## Why this unit matters

Make Product slow and observe the cascading effects. Add deadlines, isolation and circuit-breaker reasoning; compare historical Hystrix with Sentinel and modern alternatives.

The same shop remains the anchor: Product owns catalogue information, User owns customer information, and Order coordinates checkout. Read each chapter in order to see which new requirement motivates the next design decision.

## Lessons

1. **[Overload, Resource Isolation, and Cascading Failure](overload-and-isolation.qmd)**
2. **[Netflix Hystrix: Circuit Breaking](hystrix-basics.qmd)**
3. **[Hystrix Monitoring and Internals](hystrix-internals.qmd)**
4. **[Sentinel: Service Protection](sentinel-service-protection.qmd)**

## Learning objective

After this unit, describe the dependency or operational problem **before** naming a framework; draw the relevant call/event path; state the failure mode and trade-off; and explain how the concept applies to a small TypeScript or NestJS service.

## Mathematical Abstraction

Resilience applies constraints to admitted load and dependency failure.

$$
\lambda_{\rm admitted}\leq\lambda_{\rm offered},\qquad C_{\rm active}\leq C_{\max}
$$

$\lambda$ denotes rate and $C$ concurrent requests. These are policy limits, not guarantees that a failed downstream service will recover.
